guidance.summary: Meta guides Q4 2026 revenue of $73-76 billion, raises its 2026 total expense outlook to $175-179 billion to include the legal charge, narrows 2026 capex to $135-145 billion, expects Reality Labs losses of $18-19 billion in 2026 narrowing to around $15 billion in 2027, and anticipates strong revenue growth and continued aggressive investment in 2027.

guidance.sentence: We expect fourth quarter 2026 total revenue to be in the range of $73-76 billion.
We now expect full year 2026 total expenses to be in the range of $175-179 billion.
Excluding the third quarter legal charge, we continue to expect 2026 operating income to be above 2025 operating income.
At a segment level, we now expect Reality Labs losses to decline compared to 2025 to a range of $18-19 billion.
We anticipate 2026 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, to be in the range of $135-145 billion, narrowed from our prior outlook of $130-145 billion.
Absent any changes to our tax landscape, we expect our fourth quarter 2026 tax rate to be between 15-17%.

Looking beyond 2026, we are still developing our budget and capacity plans for next year, but we expect to continue investing aggressively to support both our core business and emerging AI initiatives.

Looking ahead, although we are not providing a full-year 2027 revenue outlook, the benefits our AI investments are delivering to the core business, combined with emerging opportunities from model advances and product launches, position us to sustain strong overall revenue growth throughout 2027.

Separately, we remain focused on improving Reality Labs profitability and expect losses to narrow next year to around $15 billion as we reallocate investment toward other priority areas, primarily AI.

sentences: Our guidance assumes foreign currency is an approximately 1% headwind to year-over-year total revenue growth, based on current exchange rates.

writeup.headline: Meta rates Hold: strong growth and balance sheet offset by a weak price trend and full valuation.
writeup.thesis: Meta scores 57, a Hold, with fundamentals pulling up and price action and valuation pulling down. Growth is strong, with TTM revenue growth of 27.5% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 26.1% year on year, though growth slowed by 1.9 pp from the previous quarter. Quality is high, with an 81.0% gross margin and a 32.9% operating margin and the diluted share count flat year on year, and the balance sheet scores 91 with net debt at 0.04 times FCF. Valuation scores 33: in absolute terms P/FCF of 55.7x is high and the FCF yield sits 3.2 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, reflecting an 11.9% FCF margin squeezed by heavy capex. Against its own history the stock is near the middle overall, but P/FCF is more expensive than at 60 of the last 61 month-ends, while the trend score of 31 reflects the price 20.2% below its 52-week high and shares 16.5 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days.
key_risks: Heavy AI spending: 2026 capex of $135-145 billion and signalled aggressive 2027 investment keep free cash flow thin relative to revenue.
EU and UK antitrust pushback on new commercial terms, plus the FTC appeal and youth-harm legal exposures.
Reality Labs losses expected at $18-19 billion in 2026, narrowing only to around $15 billion in 2027.
Weak price momentum, with shares 18.1 pp behind QQQ over the last 126 trading days.
Further slowing in revenue growth after it slowed by 1.9 pp from the previous quarter.
what_would_change: An 8-point score gain would reach Buy, most plausibly from a recovering price trend or a better FCF margin lifting the valuation score.
Delivering Q4 revenue at or above the $73-76 billion guide with stable growth would support the growth factor.
A 13-point score drop would mean Sell, for example if growth decelerates sharply, the trend weakens further and regulatory news turns more negative.
A higher 2027 capex outlook that further compresses free cash flow would weigh on valuation and quality.
